signals: Attended key positions per query row after the causal and sliding-window masks (positions).
Device elapsed time per active attention call (µs), grouped by head geometry, sequence length and prefill/decode.
attention.dense_execution.artifact: Attention parity fixture with explicit positions, valid keys, head-to-KV-head map, dtype, tolerance and expected output rows.
attention.dense_execution.consumer: Decoder integration agent and backend dispatch agent.
attention.dense_execution.proof: Compare a full forward and incremental decode against an independent masked softmax reference at the window boundary and across grouped heads.
attention.dense_execution.rsi: A short-context pass and long-context failure direct the next trial to mask, logical position and KV mapping. Tune kernels only after those checks pass.

signals: Legal candidate keys per query after index filtering (positions/query).
Candidate selection and sparse gather duration on the same device timeline (µs/call).
attention.sparse_execution.artifact: Extension fixture with candidate indices, validity mask, retained keys and reference output under the declared sparse model rule.
attention.sparse_execution.proof: Exercise duplicate, out-of-range and future indices. Compare to dense attention restricted to exactly the same allowed keys.
attention.sparse_execution.rsi: Incorrect selected indices reopen shortlist generation; correct indices with slow gather reopen layout. Keep outside the Muse target unless its architecture changes.

signals: Actual backend and kernel ID per eligible shape; count of fallback calls (calls/shape).
CPU submit-to-device-start gap and device execution time (µs/launch) with correlated clocks.
backend.execute_operators.artifact: Dispatch manifest with shape/stride/dtype guards, target architecture, fallback and tested kernel identities.
backend.execute_operators.consumer: Model operator agents, graph planner and performance lab.
backend.execute_operators.proof: Run shapes on both sides of every specialization guard, including tail shapes, and verify numerical parity and observed dispatch.
backend.execute_operators.rsi: A slow eligible shape still using fallback calls for a guard/layout check before changing kernel math; record the new image and compare again.

signals: Valid rows versus padded capacity at batch submission (rows/batch).
Context lengths and position offsets when the scheduler emits each row (tokens/sequence).
batch.execution_layout.artifact: Serialized batch plan with sequence IDs, token offsets, lengths, state handles and result-row scatter indices.
batch.execution_layout.consumer: Generation driver and per-sequence state owner.
batch.execution_layout.proof: Compare a mixed, reordered ragged batch with independent single-sequence runs and verify each output returns to the originating request.
batch.execution_layout.rsi: Wrong rows force an index-map repair; correct rows with excessive padding justify a shape-bucketing trial at matched load.

signals: Count of unresolved model, environment or metric obligations before contract release (obligations/revision).
Declared memory ceiling (bytes), intended context length (tokens) and user-facing time boundaries for each frozen workload.
compiler.engine_contract.artifact: Versioned engine contract linked to its reviewed intent brief, with checkpoint/tokenizer revisions, permitted choices and acceptance gates.
compiler.engine_contract.consumer: Workflow planning agent, independent lab and contract owner.
compiler.engine_contract.proof: Resolve conflicting constraints or issue a specific unsatisfied obligation. Validate that the frozen inputs and metric definitions suffice to reproduce a pass/fail decision.
compiler.engine_contract.rsi: Failures caused by an ambiguous unit or incompatible requirement reopen human intent review; performance data alone cannot authorize changing a gate.

signals: Newly committed positions at each prefill chunk or decode step (tokens/sequence).
Step wall time from ready batch to committed result (ms/step), separately for prefill and decode.
decode.advance_sequence.artifact: Sequence transition transcript containing prior length, input positions, state handles, emitted token and next committed length.
decode.advance_sequence.proof: Compare cached decode against full-prefix recomputation at chunk boundaries, cancellation and the first token after prefill.
decode.advance_sequence.rsi: A first mismatch after chunking points to state advancement or position mapping. Match outputs before testing new step sizes.

signals: Draft length and accepted prefix length per verification pass (tokens/pass).
Target evaluation time and rejected state discarded (ms/pass and positions/pass).
decode.speculative_execution.artifact: Extension acceptance transcript with draft proposals, verifier results, accepted prefix and state rollback positions.
decode.speculative_execution.proof: Force zero, partial and full acceptance. Compare target distributions and next-step state after a rejected suffix against a target-only reference.
decode.speculative_execution.rsi: A higher acceptance rate without saved wall time leads to a shorter draft-length trial. Wrong rollback blocks a performance claim.

signals: Rows, projection widths and accumulator dtype at each gate/up/down invocation (rows and channels).
Duration of each projection and activation at matched prefill/decode geometry (µs/call).
dense.feed_forward.artifact: Golden gated-FFN fixture with intermediate gate/up activations, down projection and declared activation/precision convention.
dense.feed_forward.proof: Compare all intermediates and final rows to independent arithmetic using signed inputs, zero rows and non-multiple tile widths.
dense.feed_forward.rsi: A first error before activation isolates projection packing; correct projections with high temporary traffic motivate a qualified fused path.

signals: Demand-to-ready time for an actually selected nonresident expert (µs/miss); split backing read, queue and device-visible completion where available.
Storage bytes read, resident-pool peak and late or unused prefetch bytes per declared decode interval (bytes).
engine.expert_streaming.artifact: Expert residency trace with model/layer/expert key, storage range, slot generation, demand, ready and last-use timestamps, plus effective byte budgets.
engine.expert_streaming.consumer: Expert FFN worker, placement agent and controlled experiment agent.
engine.expert_streaming.proof: Force cold misses, duplicate requests and slot reuse under a reduced budget. Verify exact reference bytes and logits, and ensure no slot is evicted before last use.
engine.expert_streaming.rsi: High reads with low exposed waits point away from storage tuning. Late demand stalls or duplicate fills justify a bounded cache or join-policy trial.

signals: Elapsed clean build and clean first boot to readiness (s/build and s/boot).
Image, compiled objects and staged model materials by identity and on-disk size (bytes).
factory.builder.artifact: Build receipt with source revision, toolchain, flags, binary/image digest, external model mounts, launch command and build logs.
factory.builder.consumer: Lab execution and release decision owners.
factory.builder.proof: Rebuild from the pinned closure, explain any nondeterministic digest and clean-start the handed-off image with its declared dependencies.
factory.builder.rsi: A different runtime library or stale binary reopens the build closure before attributing a measured change to the proposed source edit.

signals: Coverage of modified obligations by focused tests (covered/required cases); candidate source identity per test.
Unsupported layouts, fallback cases or failing checkpoints identified at integration (cases/revision).
factory.source_integration.artifact: Reviewable source patch, hook and ABI mapping, expected selected path, regression tests and rollback revision.
factory.source_integration.proof: Run through the normal call path, perform a negative/fallback case and verify expected code engagement. Repeat the pre-existing reference case.
factory.source_integration.rsi: If an edit fails to engage, repair the hook or configuration first. If engagement changes numerics, return the first divergent fixture to the owner.

signals: Unbound inputs and unmet evidence gates after source inspection (obligations/work order).
Completed, retried and blocked CC invocations per contract revision (invocations).
factory.workflow_planning.artifact: Artifact dependency plan, pinned current-state inventory and scoped work orders with source owner, inputs, outputs and retry budget.
factory.workflow_planning.consumer: JiuwenSwarm implementing agents, builder and contract owner.
factory.workflow_planning.proof: Trace every required delivery artifact back to an admitted provider, including the empty-tree case. Exercise repair without rerunning unrelated qualified jobs.
factory.workflow_planning.rsi: A measured failure reopens the smallest dependent job chain. A missing external supplier or changed requirement returns to the contract owner.

signals: Graph cache misses, captures and replays per shape/state key (counts).
Host submission and device elapsed time for matched eager and replay runs (µs/step).
graph.lower_capture_replay.artifact: Execution-plan manifest with shape guards, graph key, buffer-address lifetime and reference/replay equivalence cases.
graph.lower_capture_replay.consumer: Backend operator owners and generation driver.
graph.lower_capture_replay.proof: Vary batch shapes and addresses after capture. Require eager fallback or a valid recapture and compare outputs with uncaptured execution.
graph.lower_capture_replay.rsi: Correct replay with little end-to-end change directs investigation toward other waits; rising recaptures suggest a narrower eligible shape set.

signals: Transferred KV payload and exposed demand wait by tier (bytes/page and µs/page fault).
Dirty, in-flight and reusable pages when a migration completes (pages).
memory.kv_tiering.artifact: Logical-page migration log with original/target handle, version, completion fence, reader count and reclamation state.
memory.kv_tiering.consumer: KV allocator, scheduler and tiered-cache worker.
memory.kv_tiering.proof: Delay completion during a read, abort a migration and reuse an old slot. Require correct page identity and equivalent logits after recovery.
memory.kv_tiering.rsi: High migration traffic with little capacity benefit warrants adjusting watermarks or disabling tiering for that workload.

signals: Reusable prefix length at admission and actually skipped prompt work (tokens/request).
Pinned shared pages and eviction/reclamation lag after session retirement (pages and ms).
memory.reusable_sessions.artifact: Prefix/session reuse record binding token prefix, tokenizer/model identity, positional state and shared page ownership.
memory.reusable_sessions.proof: Try changed prompts, model or adapter revisions, siblings and evicted sessions. Reuse only compatible prefixes and match uncached continuation.
memory.reusable_sessions.rsi: Many index hits with few skipped tokens point to unusable prefix boundaries; false matches require identity repair before policy changes.

signals: Simultaneously live allocations by owner and lifetime (bytes at timestamp); include high-water mark.
Requested versus committed backing and reusable workspace at safe release points (bytes/arena).
memory.runtime_arenas.artifact: Arena layout and lifetime report keyed by physical backing, tensor owner and completion fence.
memory.runtime_arenas.consumer: Placement, backend and build qualification agents.
memory.runtime_arenas.proof: Allocate a pressure fixture with overlapping asynchronous consumers. Verify no premature reuse or double counting of shared physical pages.
memory.runtime_arenas.rsi: Use the live allocation at peak to choose between workspace reuse, smaller tiles or reduced concurrent state before lowering model quality.

signals: Occupied, reserved and reclaimed KV blocks through append and retirement (pages/sequence).
Logical position, physical block and byte offset per boundary fixture (tokens, pages and bytes).
memory.sequence_kv.artifact: Page map with KV dtype/layout, per-sequence positions, valid length, sharing/ownership and release evidence.
memory.sequence_kv.consumer: Attention kernel, generation driver and scheduler.
memory.sequence_kv.proof: Cross a page boundary and sliding-window rollover, cancel a request, then reuse its pages for another sequence and compare cached vs full logits.
memory.sequence_kv.rsi: Capacity failures with many reserved but unused pages motivate block-size or reservation changes; stale positions require correctness repair.

signals: Assignments before packing and after inverse gathering (rows/token and rows/expert).
Bytes moved by pack/gather and device time per routing histogram (bytes/batch and µs/batch).
merge.expert_contributions.artifact: Forward expert offsets, packed row IDs, inverse token/choice map and aligned weights with a reference reduction fixture.
merge.expert_contributions.consumer: Expert FFN worker, residual layer and routing verifier.
merge.expert_contributions.proof: Use tagged rows with k>1, multiple tokens choosing the same expert, empty experts and nonuniform weights. Compare the packed/reduced result to direct per-token summation.
merge.expert_contributions.rsi: Lost assignments isolate grouping; preserved IDs with wrong values isolate inverse mapping, weight alignment or duplicate scaling. Requalify before pack fusion.

signals: Layer identity and hidden-state geometry at each norm, sublayer and residual boundary (layer index, rows and channels).
First divergent hidden value and per-layer max absolute error compared with the checkpoint reference (value units).
model.decoder_architecture.artifact: Decoder wiring manifest with ordered blocks, normalization convention, residual joins, optional architecture branches and per-boundary reference activations.
model.decoder_architecture.proof: Verify post/pre-norm order, epsilon, residual scaling and repeated-layer indexing on a short forward trace with independently computed checkpoints.
model.decoder_architecture.rsi: The first divergent boundary localizes the next investigation. Preserve the passing prefix while changing just that block.

signals: Requested vocabulary IDs, out-of-range rejections and gathered row geometry (IDs, failures and channels/token).
Embedding gather elapsed time and bytes read by token shape (µs/batch and bytes).
model.embedding_service.artifact: Embedding binding manifest with vocabulary ordering, tensor shape/stride, index axis, scaling and golden rows.
model.embedding_service.proof: Gather edge IDs, repeated IDs and reordered rows. Verify exact expected vectors or declared tolerances and reject invalid IDs.
model.embedding_service.rsi: If different token IDs map correctly but the chosen ID is wrong, inspect the tokenizer; mismatches in the same row identify a tensor bind or scale problem.

signals: Selected expert IDs, aligned weights and normalization sum at router exit (IDs/token, unitless weights).
Expert selection histogram and selector device duration grouped by layer, batch shape, E and k (assignments/expert and µs/call).
model.expert_routing.artifact: Pinned routing fixture with input scores, selection rule, expected IDs and weights, eligible fast-path geometry and tie policy.
model.expert_routing.consumer: Packing and expert streaming agents; independent MoE verifier.
model.expert_routing.proof: Use a hand-evaluated fixture covering ties, shapes at the dispatch boundary and the actual checkpoint scoring/normalization rule. Compare IDs, weights and downstream output.
model.expert_routing.rsi: A histogram imbalance alone cannot justify modifying the model route. Use it to choose grouping or residency policies; numerical mismatch reopens the selector.

signals: Final hidden and output dimensions and vocabulary rank of golden tokens (channels, vocabulary entries and ranks).
Max logit difference and head projection time at selected rows (logit units and µs/row).
model.logit_head.artifact: Projection fixture with input hidden states, head tensor identity, tied-weight policy, vocabulary order and expected logit rows.
model.logit_head.proof: Compare full and last-row-only evaluation, padded vocabulary rows and any tied-weight binding against an independent projection.
model.logit_head.rsi: A correct hidden vector with shifted token rankings identifies head layout or vocabulary order; optimize row selection after parity.

signals: Correlated request/sequence/layer/stream identifiers and timestamp domain at instrumented boundaries (counts and ns or µs).
Unpaired or dropped events and matched uninstrumented/instrumented interval durations (events and ms/run).
observability.runtime_events.artifact: Optional instrumentation map and trace sample specifying event definitions, clock domain, coverage, overhead and build flags; optional NVTX ranges connect to external profilers.
observability.runtime_events.consumer: Controlled experiment agent and component owners tracing specific stalls.
observability.runtime_events.proof: Verify start/end matching, thread/stream correlation and finite overhead at the actual target. Record unavailable events and compare with tracing disabled.
observability.runtime_events.rsi: Select additional event points only when the current trace cannot separate competing explanations. Recheck the candidate on an uninstrumented timing run.

signals: Sent and received expert rows and bytes per peer at dispatch and combine (rows/rank and bytes/rank).
Collective completion wait at each expert owner (µs/dispatch or combine).
parallel.expert_exchange.artifact: Extension exchange transcript with split sizes, logical and physical expert ownership, token tags and reverse permutation.
parallel.expert_exchange.consumer: Distributed expert dispatcher and inverse-gather agent.
parallel.expert_exchange.proof: Force empty and uneven peer splits, permute rank-local rows and compare restored tokens with single-device evaluation.
parallel.expert_exchange.rsi: Imbalanced bytes across ranks motivate expert placement or padding changes. A mismatched inverse map returns to exchange correctness.

signals: Shard payload and collective ordering per rank (bytes/collective and sequence IDs).
Exposed communication latency and cross-rank skew from ready to completion (µs/collective).
parallel.model_execution.artifact: Extension topology and shard manifest with collective schedule, peer transports, layout and any live-state handoff protocol.
parallel.model_execution.consumer: Placement, distributed execution and target verification agents.
parallel.model_execution.proof: Compare output with an unsharded reference; exercise unequal local sizes and verify transferred state readiness before the next decode step.
parallel.model_execution.rsi: Correct reductions with exposed waits motivate changing shard axes or overlapping communication. Keep multi-rank work outside the single-device release.

signals: Capacity budget and measured peak by unique physical pool (bytes), including reserved headroom and storage-backed ranges.
Transferred bytes and page faults while executing each placed partition (bytes/phase and faults/phase).
placement.partition_model.artifact: Placement and residency budget for weights, KV, staging, workspace and runtime; include addressability, storage paths, target model and rejection limits.
placement.partition_model.consumer: Loader, expert streamer, arena owner and scheduler.
placement.partition_model.proof: Request an infeasible live tile and reject or select a legal alternative. On unified memory count shared pages once and confirm measured high-water behavior.
placement.partition_model.rsi: Observed headroom or fault behavior changes the next tile/residency allocation. Keep a failure trace and compare identical workload boundaries.

signals: Precision and recall against later actual demand on a time-separated holdout (fractions), measured before residency filtering.
Hint-to-demand lead time, useful and wasted transfer traffic (µs/hint and bytes/run).
routing.forecast_expert_demand.artifact: Versioned predictor, time-available input definition, ordered forecast/demand trace and hint-budget evaluation.
routing.forecast_expert_demand.consumer: Streaming policy agent and controlled experiment evaluator.
routing.forecast_expert_demand.proof: Use no future-token features. Force wrong and late predictions and require exact authoritative routing and equal outputs. Compare against no-prefetch on target.
routing.forecast_expert_demand.rsi: High accuracy without saved demand wait suggests hints target already-resident experts or arrive late; change the hint policy or disable it.

signals: Logits, allowed-set size, token probability and RNG counter at sampling boundary (logit units, tokens, probability, draws/request).
Sampling phase elapsed time and rejected constraint candidates by strategy (µs/token and count/token).
sampling.select_tokens.artifact: Sampling-policy fixture with filter order, seed, per-request RNG state, logits and expected deterministic IDs or distribution bounds.
sampling.select_tokens.proof: Verify greedy ties and reproducible seeded draws under batch reorder. Check probabilities on tiny stochastic distributions and constrained outputs.
sampling.select_tokens.rsi: Divergent tokens with matching logits direct the next check to filter order, allowed set and RNG ownership before changing model operators.

signals: Time from accepted request to first scheduled work and subsequent ready-to-run delay (ms/request and ms/step).
Admitted token count, active slots, KV credits and queue depth at each scheduling decision (tokens, slots, pages and requests).
scheduler.request_lifecycle.artifact: Decision trace covering queue admission, token budget, batch assignment, cancellation, completion and resource return.
scheduler.request_lifecycle.consumer: Batch builder, state allocator and performance experiment agent.
scheduler.request_lifecycle.proof: Replay mixed prompt lengths, overload and cancellation. Check bounded reservations, absence of starvation under declared policy and single release per request.
scheduler.request_lifecycle.rsi: Long waits with free credits suggest admission or CPU dispatch; saturated credits instead point to placement or concurrency limits. Test one change under the same offered load.

signals: Committed recurrent-state length and snapshots at reset, restore and branch (positions/sequence); hidden-state size (bytes/sequence).
Per-transition numerical error against reference recurrence (state value units).
sequence.recurrent_execution.artifact: Extension state transition fixture with model keys, sequence identity, initial state and expected carried tensors.
sequence.recurrent_execution.proof: Compare sequential replay with chunked execution; switch and resume two sequences and verify reset does not leak previous state.
sequence.recurrent_execution.rsi: Errors only after reuse identify state ownership, while first-step errors point to recurrence arithmetic. Keep extension out of Muse baseline.

signals: Transport acceptance, engine submit, first emitted byte and terminal event on a common host clock (ms/request).
Completed, rejected, cancelled and broken streams by finish condition (requests/observation interval).
serving.request_gateway.artifact: Protocol fixture with typed request identity, ordered response events, cancellation and finish status, plus effective serving interface.
serving.request_gateway.consumer: Scheduler, output codec and benchmark client.
serving.request_gateway.proof: Split output across chunks, cancel mid-generation and reconnect as supported. Check ordered emission and exactly one terminal disposition including failures.
serving.request_gateway.rsi: High client TTFT with short engine TTFT isolates protocol buffering or upstream queueing. Re-run the same client workload after the proposed change.

signals: Encoded ID count at model ingress and committed/decoded ID count at output (tokens/request).
Encoding and incremental decode time, bytes buffered at incomplete UTF-8 boundaries (µs/request, µs/token and bytes/stream).
tokenizer.prepare_request.artifact: Pinned vocabulary, tokenizer and template identities with bidirectional golden request/response fixtures.
tokenizer.prepare_request.consumer: Gateway, scheduler, embedding worker and output writer.
tokenizer.prepare_request.proof: Match exact prompt IDs, special IDs and token count; verify incremental decode of multibyte and stop-boundary cases against the same complete token stream.
tokenizer.prepare_request.rsi: Wrong model answers with good internal numerics trigger a prompt-ID comparison; correct committed tokens with damaged text trigger an output codec test.

signals: Active adapter identity, rank and resident delta footprint at each request bind (ID, rank and bytes).
Load or switch latency and output difference for base/adapter pairs (ms/switch and tensor units).
weights.adapter_binding.artifact: Extension adapter manifest with target parameter mapping, scaling, lifetime and request-scoped selection fixture.
weights.adapter_binding.consumer: Weight loader and adapter-aware execution agent.
weights.adapter_binding.proof: Alternate base and adapter requests in one batch, reject incompatible shapes and verify independent reference deltas without leakage.
weights.adapter_binding.rsi: Repeated load stalls motivate a bounded adapter cache; wrong-request deltas require an ownership fix before tuning.

signals: Declared bytes per packed block, decoded element count and absolute error against the same-format reference (bytes/block, elements/block and value units).
Decode/repack duration at the tested layout and dtype (µs/block group).
weights.decode_blocks.artifact: Format-specific golden raw bytes, scale/zero metadata, reconstructed values and kernel-layout contract.
weights.decode_blocks.consumer: Loader, matmul implementer and quantization evaluator.
weights.decode_blocks.proof: Compare signed extrema, scale boundaries, tail blocks and malformed inputs against an independent decoder for that exact format. Compare downstream matmul as well.
weights.decode_blocks.rsi: Bit-level error reopens layout decoding; acceptable local reconstruction but poor model quality belongs to calibration/representation selection under a frozen task.

signals: Mapped or read byte ranges, tensors bound and missing or mismatched entries at readiness (bytes/shard, tensors and errors).
Startup interval from load initiation to complete validated bindings (s/load) under a declared cache state.
weights.load_checkpoint.artifact: Validated weight inventory with tensor names, shapes, dtypes, offsets, file sizes, checksums and persistent storage identity.
weights.load_checkpoint.consumer: Decoder binder, placement agent and streamer.
weights.load_checkpoint.proof: Test split or truncated files, missing shards, duplicate names and a correctly loaded small checkpoint. Ensure all referenced ranges lie within their file.
weights.load_checkpoint.rsi: Identify whether startup time belongs to metadata checks, data reads or first-use conversion before parallelizing load or changing storage.

signals: Packed bytes and overhead by tensor including scales, alignment and index metadata (bytes/tensor).
Reconstruction error distribution and held-out logit or task-quality delta versus the pinned higher-precision reference (value units, logit units or percentage points).
weights.prepare_artifact.artifact: Versioned converted model with source/format identities, quantization and calibration recipe, tensor-wise precision choices, quality report and independent decode fixture.
weights.prepare_artifact.consumer: Loader, block decoder and controlled quality evaluator.
weights.prepare_artifact.proof: Use held-out calibration-independent text, verify tensor identities and byte accounting, then evaluate model numerics and task quality at matched decoding settings.
weights.prepare_artifact.rsi: A smaller artifact with unacceptable quality triggers per-tensor sensitivity analysis or a higher-precision exception, followed by the same held-out tests.

signals: Active rows and selected compute variant by layer/expert (rows/expert and kernel ID); attach dtype and matrix geometry.
Time from expert weights ready to completion, and reference error at gate/up/down boundaries (µs/expert group and tensor units).
model.expert_ffn.artifact: Expert arithmetic fixture with grouped rows, protected weight handles, dimensions, activation, expected projections and grouped output order.
model.expert_ffn.consumer: Routed row gather/reducer, kernel writer and lab verifier.
model.expert_ffn.proof: Compare empty, singleton and uneven expert groups against independent per-expert arithmetic including signed gates. Track the weight handle through final device consumption.
model.expert_ffn.rsi: If the first mismatch is inside projection, inspect weight/scale layout; correct math with poor throughput directs a grouped-vs-individual kernel trial by row count.

signals: Quality gate, wall time, client TTFT/ITL, throughput, bytes moved and peak live memory for the frozen prompt/concurrency/cache configuration (quality units, ms, output tokens/s and bytes).
Record valid, failed and excluded attempts by image/target and paired baseline-to-candidate effect with sample count and uncertainty (runs, ratio or percentage points).
factory.controlled_experiment.artifact: Trial manifest and evidence bundle with question, baseline/candidate revisions and digests, independent oracle, resource budget, raw logs, controls, exclusions, verdict and reproduction command.
factory.controlled_experiment.consumer: Planner deciding repair, release reviewer and agents preparing the next bounded experiment.
factory.controlled_experiment.proof: Verify that a deliberately wrong result fails, reproduce a baseline and preserve partial failures. For quantized candidates compare memory and speed with a separately frozen numerical/task-quality gate on held-out text.
factory.controlled_experiment.rsi: Accept, reject, request confirmation or identify the smallest unresolved hypothesis. A speed gain cannot override a failed numerical or quality gate. Feed the identified owner and reproduction artifacts back into planning.

signals: Open scope-changing questions per brief revision.
Count of requirements with recorded provenance and review status.
compiler.intent_brief.artifact: A versioned, reviewed intent brief with the original request, constraints, preferences and unresolved decisions.
compiler.intent_brief.proof: Trace each captured requirement to the request or a reviewed clarification. Flag unresolved choices that would change the requested engine.
compiler.intent_brief.rsi: Reopen intent capture when the requested outcome or constraints change. Preserve the prior brief and its review history.
